source_reviews.independent_solution: Incoming energy crosses the solid wall mainly by conduction; the inner wall can heat room air by contact conduction and convection, with other surface exchanges possible. Hot air entering an open window carries energy by convection. Sunlight transmitted through glass carries energy by radiation and commonly warms surfaces that later heat room air by conduction/convection.

mathematics.independent_solution: Radiation does not need transported material. Solid walls conduct and subsequently heat air by conduction/convection. Incoming hot air convects. option_checks.evidence: Electromagnetic radiation crosses the near-vacuum without a bulk stream of matter from Sun to Earth.

Heat crosses an ordinary solid wall predominantly by conduction; contact with the warm inner wall and motion of heated air allow conduction and convection into the room air. No exclusive claim rules out other exchanges.
The explicitly moving hot air carries energy with mass flow. That is convection; labelling it conduction and excluding convection reverses the mechanism.
Energy of sunlight transmitted through window glass is radiation. Absorbing indoor surfaces can subsequently conduct heat to adjacent air and drive air convection.
With no contact and no direct hot-air stream at the side of the flame, absorbed radiation can be the main direct heating mechanism. 'Can mainly' does not falsely exclude every other exchange.
A wind or circulating warm air can reach someone at the side without contact. Unchecked airflow makes the claim of complete exclusion of convection false.
